topic: Discrete Convolutions: From Image Blurring to Feature Detection

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The 'Moving Window' Concept
lecture_lines: Convolution is a sliding window operator.
Imagine a 3x3 filter passing over pixels.
Multiply pixel values by filter weights.
Sum results to produce new pixel value.
animations: Display 3x3 red (#FF0000) square outline around top-left 3x3 pixels.
Animate red outline sliding row-by-row across the 5x5 grid.
Show math symbol: Input (color: #FFFFFF) * Filter (color: #FF0000) = Output (color: #00FFFF).
Flash the output cell when window moves to a new position.

sections.title: Mathematical Mechanics (Graphical Representation)
lecture_lines: Sliding across input produces output sequence.
animations: Animate sum of products moving into output sequence (color: #00FFFF).
Transition from input to output using dashed arrow (color: #AAAAAA).

sections.title: Application: Feature Detection in Computer Vision
lecture_lines: Positive and negative values identify edges.
High contrast yields strong signal response.
animations: Display edge detection kernel (color: #FF5500) moving across.
Show resulting feature map (color: #00FF00) emphasizing vertical edges.

sections.title: Real-World Integration: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)
lecture_lines: AI learns optimal filter weights automatically.
animations: Show three stacked 2D grids representing layers.
Animate red kernel sliding across each layer sequentially.
